extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, test laboratories, compliance engineers, and regulatory staff involved with FMVSS No. 210 anchorage strength testing
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and laboratory procedures for testing seat belt anchorage strength under FMVSS No. 210, including use/positioning of body blocks, Force Application Device (FAD) options, preload and hold conditions, seat and belt setup, and compliance timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positioning device use
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA will not require use of a dedicated positioning device when developing or placing the body blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency research showed simple fixtures can aid initial body block placement but required preload positions can be achieved without such aids; test laboratories are given flexibility to use whatever method they prefer to reach preload positions. NHTSA also decided not to revise the body block design.

rubrics_metrics.name: FEA modeling for body block positioning
rubrics_metrics.description: FEA modeling is not required for positioning body blocks for FMVSS No. 210 compliance tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA and commenters concurred it would be unviable to require labs to replicate manufacturer-specific FEA positions; FEA would necessitate detailed seat information collections and impose cost/time burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment (D-ring)
rubrics_metrics.description: The shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment (D-ring) may be set to any height for regulatory testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The laboratory test procedure continues to specify the 'center position' for compliance testing contractor guidance, but for manufacturer certification the regulatory text controls and permits any height. In NHTSA's fleet study the D-ring was set to mid-height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preload force magnitude (body blocks and FAD laboratory procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preload of 1,335 N is specified to be applied to each body block (and the updated laboratory procedure will specify 1,335 N for the FAD preload attachments) for both Type 1 and Type 2 belts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically labs used 10% of target load (e.g., 2,224 N for Type 1 pelvic block). NHTSA chose 1,335 N because it is lower (preferable for lab safety) and research found no meaningful effect on body block position. The final rule specifies this preload for body blocks; the regulatory text does not specify a preload for FAD tests, but the laboratory procedure will match the 1,335 N preload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preload force duration
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific duration for how long the preload force must be applied is specified in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duration of preload may vary with laboratory equipment, personnel, seat types, and test device and is not part of the 30-second ramp-up. NHTSA believes variation in preload duration will not affect outcomes given its low magnitude and historical testing experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: No contact between body blocks during preload
rubrics_metrics.description: When testing with body blocks, there must be no contact between the body blocks while the preload force is being applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FAD testing, NHTSA assesses whether there is any contact between adjacent FAD1s before any preload is applied; if contact exists, a FAD1 is replaced with a FAD2 according to the FAD positioning procedure (S5.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test force ramp-up timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The 30-second ramp-up to reach the required test force commences after positioning and preload are completed, not during the preload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioning adjustments can be made before or during preload without affecting the 30-second ramp-up time requirement. The preload period is excluded from the 30-second interval for applying the test load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat adjustment using seat geometric reference point (SgRP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seats shall be adjusted to the rearmost normal riding or driving position using the SgRP specified by the manufacturer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rearmost normal riding or driving position includes all modes of seat adjustment (horizontal, vertical, seat back angle, seat cushion angle). NHTSA replaced the H-point procedure with SgRP so the positioning procedure applies consistently to both body blocks and FAD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat back angle specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Seat back angle (when adjustable) is to be set consistent with the manufacturer's SgRP rather than the prior H-point/SAE J826 procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously the NPRM referenced H-point measured by SAE J826 (July 1995); the final rule uses SgRP to provide a well-defined seat position familiar to manufacturers and requested by OVSC prior to testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat belt pretension and routing (remove all slack)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulatory text adopts the longstanding FMVSS No. 208 directive to 'remove all slack' when positioning the FAD/dummies and does not prescribe the specific wooden-rod procedure proposed in the NPRM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA found 'remove all slack' adequate from FMVSS No. 208 practice. For body blocks, belt tension and routing affect block placement at preload; labs may adjust tension/routing (or substitute material) when positioning blocks in the zone. In research, belts were marked at the D-ring and locked at desired length to control fore/aft position; routing on the torso block can be used to avoid interference between torso and pelvic blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hold time requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The required hold time for the required test load remains 10 seconds under FMVSS No. 210.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA did not propose to alter the 10-second hold in the NPRM. Requests (e.g., from Honda) to reduce it to 1 second were considered out of scope for this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Force application angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Forces must be initially applied at an angle not less than 5 degrees and not more than 15 degrees above the horizontal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA's study found pull angle had only a small effect on preload position (within ~33 mm across tests). A wide tolerance is retained to aid test setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a dedicated test belt
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a dedicated test belt that does not absorb energy is permitted when testing seat belt anchorages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FMVSS No. 210 S5 requires connecting the anchorage to material whose breaking strength is equal to or greater than the original webbing. Dedicated test belts (e.g., steel cable) are allowed and need no further clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing of side-facing seats
rubrics_metrics.description: Side-facing seats and seats adjustable to face any direction are subject to FMVSS No. 210 anchorage strength requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal of the 'side-facing seats' exclusion became effective December 16, 2013; NHTSA clarifies the standard applies to seats that face any direction or can be adjusted to face any direction. The seat reference plane (parallel to the direction the seat faces through the SgRP) defines the direction in which specified test forces are applied. Comments on appropriateness of side-facing test direction were outside this rule's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance options: FAD optional with body blocks retained
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers may certify using either the Force Application Device (FAD) or the current body blocks (with specified zones); the FAD is adopted as an optional test device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both compliance options allows manufacturers to choose based on familiarity, cost, lead time, and harmonization concerns. The body blocks have a long compliance history; FAD offers potential advantages (ease of testing, ability to test 4-point belts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block placement zones
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule specifies zones within which the agency may position the body blocks at preload for compliance testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These zones clarify and restrict agency discretion compared to the previous standard which did not specify placement. Manufacturers must certify compliance at any position within the applicable zone. The zone-based placement may deviate from ECE R14 pre-test positioning requirements (e.g., pushing pelvic block into seatback) but NHTSA considers the deviation necessary for enforceability and to avoid affecting seat/anchorage performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: International harmonization and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA considered harmonization with international standards (ECE R14, Transport Canada TSD 210, ADR 05, SAE J384) but will proceed with U.S. amendments while providing compliance options to preserve harmonization opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FAD was developed independently and is not adopted abroad; other standards mirror FMVSS No.210 body blocks. NHTSA may allow manufacturers to continue using body blocks to maintain alignment with other countries. Initiation of a GTR would not preclude this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead time for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A two-year lead time is provided for manufacturers to comply with the amended procedures for both body blocks (zones) and the FAD; multi-stage manufacturers and alterers receive one additional year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA believes two years is reasonable given body blocks' longstanding use and the clarification nature of zones; providing both options also alleviates lead-time concerns for FAD procurement and familiarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD contact assessment and replacement (S5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before applying preload in FAD testing, assess for contact between adjacent FAD1s; if contact exists replace FAD1 with FAD2 per S5.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pre-preload check differs from body-block preload requirement (no contact during preload) and is part of the FAD positioning procedure to avoid interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretest photographs and angle measurements at preload
rubrics_metrics.description: At preload, laboratories historically take photographs and measurements of the load application angle; the updated laboratory procedure will similarly specify photographic and measurement verification at the specified preload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longstanding laboratory practice used a 10% preload and photographic documentation to verify pull angle and chain tension. The updated procedure will continue this verification practice at the 1,335 N preload level.
